_note: Each case runs one skill against a fresh copy of examples/fixture-os and then reads the filesystem. Assertions are deliberately structural -- what got written, where, and what stayed untouched -- because that is what the cross-cutting rules actually claim. Two checks run on every case regardless: raw/ stays append-only, and a usage/log.md row gets appended. The frame answers a skill's clarifying question rather than stopping at it: two cases in the first full run wrote nothing at all because corp-os-intake and corp-os-brief correctly refused to proceed without a person -- intake asks when a type is ambiguous, brief asks for a window when meta.json holds no prior brief. Both were doing exactly what their skill says. Reading that as failure would have 'fixed' two skills that were right; the harness was wrong. Cases carry an optional `fixture` -- examples/fixture-os is the shipped default shape, examples/fixture-register is a jobs-off OS with renamed vocabulary and a hand-maintained source layer. The irreversible-path cases run against the register fixture because that is where a role mistake actually costs something.

cases.prompt:
Here's the notes from this morning's call with Northwind, add them to my OS.

[Dana Okafor] We're not going to be able to justify the renewal at the current seat count. It isn't the product, it's the math.
[me] Is that a budget thing or a value thing?
[Dana Okafor] Budget. We froze headcount in July and the seats we're paying for aren't all active.
[me] If the seats tracked active users instead, does that change it?
[Dana Okafor] That would change it, yes. I'd need to see the numbers.

expect_added.name: raw file written for the pasted material
expect_added.why: intake's whole job is filing source material into the append-only layer; a run that only talks about it has done nothing

expect_added.name: proposal file written before claims were presented
expect_added.why: the gate is persisted, not conversational -- a proposal that lives only in chat leaves no record of what the gate saw

expect_changed.name: INDEX.md updated in the same pass
expect_changed.why: the index describes what is in raw/, and that is already true the moment the file lands; waiting on the claims decision is a bug, not caution

expect_changed.name: meta.json recounted
expect_changed.why: hand-incremented counts are where drift enters, and a wrong count poisons the scan contract for every later run

cases.answers: it's a transcript from a call I was on, file it as one -- and yes, go ahead and propose whatever findings it earns
cases._note: Dropped a 'INDEX.md contains the word northwind' assertion. It was testing the slug the run happened to choose, not the rule. The generic check -- every newly added raw file is reachable from INDEX.md by name -- says what the scan contract actually requires and applies to every case.

expect_added.name: proposal file written before anything was presented

expect_untouched.name: the disabled glossary layer was not created
expect_untouched.why: config says glossary is disabled; a skill that scaffolds a layer the config turned off is not reading config first

expect_contains.name: the person's own vocabulary is used, not the plugin's
expect_contains.why: config renames claim to finding here; a run that never opened config.json will not know that

expect_untouched.name: no raw material was written
expect_untouched.why: a standing review reads; a review that writes source material has misunderstood what it was asked

cases.prompt: I've got the Northwind renewal call in an hour. What do we know that bears on it, and what don't we know?

expect_untouched.name: nothing entered the derived layer
expect_untouched.why: recall answers and proposes; a recall run that writes claims has skipped the gate entirely

expect_untouched.name: no raw material was written
expect_untouched.why: answering a question is not capture

cases._note: Dropped the blunt 'jobs untouched' assertion after the first run. These runs are told the person confirms, so a write to a job's evidence list is legitimate -- what is not legitimate is a write with no proposal behind it, and the universal gate check covers that for every case. Asserting 'must not write' under a frame that grants confirmation was testing the frame, not the skill.

cases.prompt: Is any of this still accurate? Sweep it and tell me what I shouldn't be trusting.

expect_untouched.name: no raw material was written
expect_untouched.why: the sweep reads claims and interrogates; it has no reason to write source material

expect_contains.name: the unsourced entry was handled as its own bucket
expect_contains.why: CL-0002 has citation `no source`; mixing it into the overdue bucket produces a backlog nobody can clear, which is how people learn to skip the sweep

cases.prompt: Brief me on where things stand.

expect_untouched.name: nothing entered the derived layer
expect_untouched.why: a brief reports; it does not create knowledge

expect_changed.name: meta.json history records the brief and its window
expect_changed.why: the next brief starts from that date; without it every brief covers the whole corpus and stops being a brief

cases.answers: brief on everything since the last pull on 2026-08-20 -- there is no prior brief recorded, so that is the window

cases.prompt: Nobody's confident the derived side still reflects what's in raw. Regenerate it from source.
cases.answers: yes, go ahead, regenerate everything that's derivable — and don't ask me again mid-run, just do it and report what changed

expect_untouched.name: the hand-maintained source layer survived
expect_untouched.why: playbooks/ is declared role: source. It looks derived -- prose, no citations, no obvious origin in raw/ -- and a rebuild that overwrites it destroys work with nothing to restore from. This is the one failure mode in the whole system that loses data rather than degrading quality, which is why the fixture plants it

expect_untouched.name: the raw archive was not rewritten
expect_untouched.why: a rebuild reads raw/ wholesale; that is the one operation licensed to. It is never licensed to write there

expect_changed.name: meta.json carries a dated history entry for the rebuild
expect_changed.why: a rebuild that leaves no trace of having run is indistinguishable from drift the next time someone looks

expect_unmodified.name: the existing proposals record was not rewritten
expect_unmodified.why: proposals/ is role: record -- an audit trail. Filing a new proposal for this rebuild is correct; rewriting or removing what is already there would edit history to match the present, which is the opposite of what a record is for

cases._note: The proposals assertion started as expect_untouched and failed a run that had done everything right: the rebuild filed its own proposal, which is what it should do. 'Not regenerated' and 'not written to at all' are different claims and the harness was making the wrong one.

cases.prompt: Our vendor agreement has a data-deletion clause — anything from Meridian correspondence has to come out after the contract ends, and that's now. Set up the retention policy and apply it to the Meridian thread.
cases.answers: yes, the obligation is the deletion clause in the Meridian MSA, and yes go ahead and carry it out — tell me what it costs before you do

expect_changed.name: entries citing the deleted source were re-cited
expect_changed.why: deleting a source file without re-citing the entries that depend on it leaves them pointing at files that do not exist -- worse than `no source`, because they still look sourced and nothing downstream can tell the difference

expect_changed.name: config.json records the policy and the obligation
expect_changed.why: `reason` is required on a delete policy and should name the obligation; 'housekeeping' is not a reason to destroy source material

expect_changed.name: meta.json logs what was destroyed and under what obligation
expect_changed.why: the log is the only remaining evidence that the material ever existed

cases._note: allow_raw_delete flips the universal append-only check into its opposite for this case: deletion under a stated obligation is sanctioned, and a run that deleted nothing would not have exercised the sequence. Every other case still treats a removal as the violation it is.

cases.prompt: I want to send the Northwind pricing picture to our board advisor — someone outside the company. Clean it up first.
cases.answers: external, outside the company entirely, and yes go ahead and produce the cleaned version

expect_untouched.name: the originals were not modified in place
expect_untouched.why: redaction produces a copy; a redaction skill that edits the source has quietly destroyed the unredacted version, and the person will not find out until they need it

expect_untouched.name: raw was not touched
expect_untouched.why: raw is append-only and must survive redaction untouched -- it is the thing the cleaned copy was derived from

expect_added.name: two outputs, not one — a cleaned copy and its private log
expect_added.why: redaction produces two files and the log is the one that goes missing. Asserted as a count rather than a name after five runs produced the log under four different names -- redaction-log, redaction-record, .redaction-log, .LEDGER -- and once not at all. The naming variance is itself the finding: a stated filename is not achieving determinism here

cases._note: Three runs, three locations, a log every time -- including one that named it 'redaction-record'. The skill keeps its recommended path so the person has somewhere consistent to look, but the check now asserts what actually matters: a private log exists, locally, alongside the cleaned copy.
